publication_redaction.changes: Private workstation receiver address in command_catalog replaced with RFC 5737 documentation address 192.0.2.30; original artifact retained privately outside the repository.

scope: Finite Milestone 1 architecture-spike evidence; not a production media engine or endurance benchmark.

capture_device.conversion_observed: Channel conversion from native mono to stereo; sample rate and S16 format were unchanged.

probe.registry_policy: GStreamer registry was created and used only in a validated mktemp directory under /tmp; GST_REGISTRY_UPDATE=no was used after the initial isolated scan.

vlc_interoperability.reason: VLC/cvlc was absent on the Pi and development host; no package was installed.

queue_isolation.interpretation: Over about 15 seconds of wall time while the slow branch drained, the one-second-per-buffer disposable branch handled 13 buffers while the independently queued stream branch delivered all 251 decoded buffers representing about 5 seconds of stream content.

warnings_and_limitations: Every finite GStreamer listener logged one SRT socket warning when the caller intentionally closed; the receivers still exited 0 after EOS.

Each LAN sender and the queue/mutation sender emitted two non-fatal gst_buffer_list_foreach critical assertions in GStreamer 1.26.2; no bus error, nonzero exit, missing decoded stream, or PTS discontinuity was observed.
FFplay ran in a cached linux/amd64 container with dummy audio on the Windows receiver; this proves receiver decoding, not audible output quality.
The runs were approximately five seconds. Endurance, interruption recovery, SRT reconnect, packet loss, recording, simultaneous monitoring, and production lifecycle behavior remain untested.
The iMM-6C is natively mono. These exact candidate representations were tested after mono-to-stereo channel conversion and must not be described as native stereo capture.
The private receiver address is retained only inside the exact executed LAN commands; no credential, SSID, or MAC address is retained.
